documents.problemStatement:
## Problem

`adv_store_cleanup action:"scan"` and `adv_store_consolidate action:"scan"` time out at the hard 10s tool ceiling (`safeExecute` DEFAULT_TOOL_TIMEOUT_MS, matched by the OpenCode SDK host) on machines with many local ADV stores.

Observed: a data-home with ~379 orphan-shard stores + ~32 drain-* stores + others (400+). `scanStoresForCleanup` (store-cleanup.ts:345) and the two per-store loops in store-consolidate.ts (lines 654, 792) iterate stores with a fully serial `for…of await` loop performing ~6 filesystem ops per store (readJsonlHashed + a redundant second readFileSafe of the same agenda.jsonl + sha256 + probeWorkerLock + probeConsolidationLedger + probeCleanupManifest). ~2,400 serial I/O ops under heavy multi-agent I/O contention exceed 10s, so the scans never return and no cleanup/consolidation can proceed.

The 10s ceiling cannot be raised (SDK host cap; rq-boundedAuthoritativeRead01 forbids raising read deadlines). The fix must make the scan structurally faster.

Out of scope: the archived/terminal change-enumeration timeout family (adv_status view:hygiene, adv_worktree_cleanup mode:archived_branches) which is owned by fixChangeEnumerationStarvation and its fast-follow.</problemStatement>
<parameter name="proposal">## Proposal

Make the store maintenance scans structurally fast enough to complete well under the 10s tool ceiling by:

1. Adding a small reusable bounded-concurrency helper `mapWithConcurrency(items, concurrency, fn)` in `plugin/src/utils/` (order-preserving, collects results, bounded to avoid EMFILE from unbounded Promise.all over hundreds of stores).
2. Replacing the serial per-store loops in `scanStoresForCleanup` (store-cleanup.ts) and both per-store loops in store-consolidate.ts with bounded-concurrency mapping.
3. Eliminating the redundant double read of `agenda.jsonl` in the cleanup scan (read the file once; derive rows/malformed/hashes and the whole-file content hash from the single read).

Behavior is otherwise unchanged: scans stay read-only, classification semantics and output (entries, warnings, flagged/candidate lists, deterministic ordering) are identical to the serial implementation — only wall-time drops by roughly the concurrency factor.</proposal>
<parameter name="agreement">## Objectives

Store maintenance scans (`adv_store_cleanup action:scan`, `adv_store_consolidate action:scan`) complete within the 10s tool ceiling on realistic large-store data-homes (400+ stores), without changing their read-only classification results.

## Success Criteria

- SC1: On a fixture with hundreds of stores, both scans complete well under the 10s tool ceiling (target: order-of-magnitude faster than serial; deterministic under fake/bounded timing in tests).
- SC2: Scan classification output (entries, warnings, flagged/candidate lists, ordering) is byte-identical to the pre-change serial implementation for the same fixture.
- SC3: Per-store I/O is bounded (no unbounded Promise.all); a large store count cannot exhaust file descriptors (no EMFILE).
- SC4: `agenda.jsonl` is read at most once per store in the cleanup scan.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: Given a data-home with N stores, when a scan runs, then per-store probing executes with bounded concurrency and results match the serial ordering/classification.
- AC2: Given the cleanup scan, when a store is classified, then agenda.jsonl is read exactly once.
- AC3: Given a very large store count, when a scan runs, then concurrency is capped and no EMFILE/descriptor exhaustion occurs.
- AC4: Given identical fixtures, when serial vs parallel results are compared, then stores/flagged/warnings/candidates are equal.

## Constraints

- C1: Scans remain strictly read-only (no mutations).
- C2: No raising of the 10s tool timeout or any read deadline (rq-boundedAuthoritativeRead01).
- C3: No new runtime dependency; helper is in-repo and unit-tested.
- C4: Do not touch the terminal/archived change-enumeration path (fixChangeEnumerationStarvation domain).

## Avoidances

- DONT1: Do not use unbounded Promise.all over all stores.
- DONT2: Do not alter classification/safety semantics (unsafe/live-lock/ledger detection must be preserved exactly).
- DONT3: Do not change execute/dry_run mutation behavior in this change (scan performance only; dry_run/execute reuse scan and inherit the speedup, but their plan/mutation logic is unchanged).
documents.design:
## Architecture

Add `plugin/src/utils/concurrency.ts` exporting `mapWithConcurrency<T, R>(items: readonly T[], concurrency: number, fn: (item: T, index: number) => Promise<R>): Promise<R[]>`:
- Bounded worker-pool over a shared index cursor; preserves input order in the results array (write `results[i]`).
- `concurrency` clamped to `[1, items.length]`; a default constant (e.g. 16) used by callers, chosen to stay well below OS descriptor limits while saturating fs I/O.
- Pure, deterministic, no timers; unit-tested for order preservation, bounded in-flight count, and error propagation.

## Changes

1. `store-cleanup.ts`:
   - Single-read refactor: a pure `analyzeAgenda(content)` helper provides jsonl analysis (rows/malformed/hashes) and the whole-file content hash from one `readFileSafe(agendaPath)`. Removes the second read at line 349.
   - `scanStoresForCleanup`: replace `for (const ref of stores)` with `mapWithConcurrency(stores, STORE_SCAN_CONCURRENCY, async (ref) => …)` returning per-store entry plus any warnings; warnings aggregated after (preserving sorted output). Classification logic unchanged.
2. `store-consolidate.ts`:
   - Both per-store loops (≈654, ≈792) converted to `mapWithConcurrency`, preserving each function's existing classification, collision detection, and output shape/order.

## Verification Contract

- Unit tests for `mapWithConcurrency`: order preservation, max in-flight ≤ concurrency, rejection propagation, empty input.
- store-cleanup scan test: large-N fixture asserting (a) parallel result deep-equals a serial reference, (b) agenda.jsonl read count == store count (spy), (c) completes fast.
- store-consolidate scan test: parallel vs serial parity on a mixed fixture, plus bounded concurrency.
- Full `pnpm run check` + targeted store suites green; real-machine `adv_store_cleanup action:scan` returns under budget as live proof.

## Non-goals

Terminal/archived change enumeration (hygiene, archived_branches) — separate ownership.

documents.executiveSummary:
## Executive Summary

### Outcome
The two operator maintenance scans — `adv_store_cleanup action:scan` and `adv_store_consolidate action:scan` — no longer time out on machines with many local ADV stores. Both were rewritten from serial per-store loops to bounded-concurrency probing, and the store-cleanup scan now reads each store's `agenda.jsonl` exactly once instead of twice.

### Why it matters
On this machine the store data-home holds 400+ stores (≈379 orphan-shard + ≈32 drain-* + others). The serial scans exceeded the hard 10-second tool ceiling (which cannot be raised — SDK cap plus `rq-boundedAuthoritativeRead01`), so operators could not inventory or clean inert store cruft at all. The consolidate scan was worst-hit because it spawned a git subprocess per store (~758 serial git spawns for 379 stores). Parallelizing to a bounded pool (16) cuts wall-time by roughly the concurrency factor while a bounded pool avoids file-descriptor exhaustion (EMFILE) that naive `Promise.all` would cause.

### What changed
- New `plugin/src/utils/concurrency.ts` — `mapWithConcurrency(items, concurrency, fn)`: order-preserving, bounded worker pool. `STORE_SCAN_CONCURRENCY=16`.
- `store-cleanup.ts`: parallelized `scanStoresForCleanup`; single-read `analyzeAgenda(content)` helper removes the redundant second file read.
- `store-consolidate.ts`: parallelized the `scanStoresForRepo` per-store loop (git identity probes + fs summary batched).
- Behavior is preserved exactly: classification, safety flags, warning order, and deterministic `project_id`-sorted output are byte-identical to the serial implementation.

### Verification
- `pnpm run check` green (schemas, typecheck, manifests, isolation, lockfile, lint, format).
- 84/84 targeted tests green: `mapWithConcurrency` unit tests (order, bounded in-flight, rejection, clamp, empty); store-cleanup large-N parity + determinism + single-read; store-consolidate 52-store parity + determinism + orphan-suspect + live-lock warning.
- CI on PR #242: 6/6 checks green.

### Risks / follow-ups
- Low risk: pure behavior-preserving refactor of read-only maintenance scans; no timeout/deadline constants touched, no new dependency, no mutation-path changes.
- Out of scope (separate ownership): the archived/terminal change-enumeration timeout family (`adv_status view:hygiene`, `adv_worktree_cleanup mode:archived_branches`) is owned by `fixChangeEnumerationStarvation` and a planned fast-follow.
- Live post-deploy `adv_store_cleanup action:scan` under-budget confirmation is pending the build+deploy+restart step.
